audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht’s Sustainable Bioscience bachelor studies ecosystems, agriculture and food through biological and Earth sciences, lab and field work, and data analysis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This 2026–2027 example illustrates the Planetary Systems concentration and one possible set of second-year electives. The UCR plan combines ecology and Earth science with biology, data and sustainability.

notes.text: Both plans cover biology, ecology, Earth systems and data analysis. Maastricht also offers dedicated courses in plant biology and food and nutrition, and specialised laboratory training. The UCR plan includes sustainable farming and related laboratory work in life science.

Maastricht combines a fixed first year, second-year electives and four collaborative research projects with a third-year concentration, design challenge and 30 EC individual thesis. UCR offers related research methods and optional independent research.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.

ENSECOL111.name: Introduction to Biodiversity
ENSECOL111.text: Introduces the diversity of living organisms, from bacteria and archaea to protists, plants, fungi and animals. Students examine evolutionary relationships, distinguishing characteristics and ecological roles. Practical work introduces microscopy, organism identification and biodiversity measurement, supported by a small project on a selected branch of the tree of life.

ENSECOL112.name: Conservation Biology
ENSECOL112.text: Examines human-driven biodiversity loss and approaches to conservation. Students study habitat destruction, overharvesting, invasive species, climate change and extinction, followed by conservation planning and species management. A local threatened-species project investigates conservation status and protection measures and develops a public-awareness flyer.

ENSECOL311.name: Marine Biology
ENSECOL311.text: Studies ecological processes in marine environments such as estuaries, rocky shores and coral reefs. Examines human impacts and includes guest lectures, lab visits, excursions and field work, culminating in an essay.

ENSECOL312.name: Sustainable Farming & Innovation
ENSECOL312.text: Discusses environmental impacts of agriculture and explores sustainable agriculture approaches such as agroecology, organic farming, conservation agriculture, precision agriculture, sustainable livestock farming, agroforestry, permaculture, crop rotation, integrated pest management and sustainable supply chains.
